[ServiceWorker] Starting Agentic Pipeline for intent: Guide me on how to apply for a driver's license by myself full process 

Yep. If you're applying in Maharashtra, you can handle the whole process yourself—no driving school or agent is required for a normal private motorcycle/car licence.

The process is basically:

Learner's Licence (LL) → learn/practise → wait at least 30 days → Driving Licence application → driving test → permanent DL

Maharashtra's official guidance confirms that you can apply for the permanent licence after 30 days from obtaining the learner's licence. 
Transport Maharashtra
+1

1. Decide which vehicle classes you need

If you want a normal bike + car licence, you'll generally be dealing with:

MCWG — Motorcycle With Gear

LMV — Light Motor Vehicle, for private cars

If you intend to drive both, select both classes when the portal offers them rather than unnecessarily doing separate applications.

For ordinary private vehicles, you need to be 18 or older. Maharashtra's official LL page confirms this eligibility. 
Transport Maharashtra

2. Keep your documents ready

Before starting, keep your Aadhaar, proof of age, proof of address, passport-size photos if required, and your mobile phone available. The Maharashtra Motor Vehicle Department lists proof of residence, proof of age, citizenship proof, photographs and the applicable fee among the LL requirements. 
Transport Maharashtra

The online process can differ somewhat depending on whether Aadhaar authentication/faceless services are available for your application, so follow what Sarathi specifically asks you to upload or present.

3. Start on the official Sarathi website

Use the Government of India's official portal:

Sarathi Parivahan

Select Maharashtra.

Once Maharashtra loads, find the option for Learner Licence → Application for New Learner Licence. The exact menu layout can change, so focus on the wording rather than the position of the button.

Do not choose "New Driving Licence" yet. That's the second stage after obtaining your LL.

4. Complete the New Learner's Licence application

You'll be given an application form. Fill in your details exactly as they appear on your official documents, especially your:

Name → DOB → address → Aadhaar/details requested → contact information → vehicle class

For bike + car, choose the appropriate motorcycle class and LMV.

After submission, save your application number. Screenshot it as well.

You'll use that number for payment, appointments, application status and other services.

5. Upload/verify documents and pay the LL fee

Complete whatever stages Sarathi shows for your application, such as document upload, photo/signature, Aadhaar authentication, fee payment and LL test/slot booking.

Maharashtra's current published fee table lists the learner's licence fee as ₹151 per vehicle class plus ₹50 test fee. Your actual payable amount should be taken from the amount Sarathi calculates for your application. 
Transport Maharashtra

Sarathi's payment system allows you to use the application number and DOB to calculate the applicable fee, make payment, verify payment status and print the receipt. 
Sarathi

Save the payment receipt.

6. Take the Learner's Licence test

The LL test is a theory/knowledge test—not the actual car/bike driving test.

Study things such as road signs, traffic signals, right of way, overtaking rules, parking rules, speed/road-safety rules and basic driver responsibilities.

Maharashtra says you need 60% correct answers to pass the preliminary LL test. If you fail, you can book another appointment and retake it. 
Transport Maharashtra

Depending on the workflow offered for your application, the test/verification may be online/faceless or may require an RTO visit.

7. Get your Learner's Licence

After passing and approval, download your LL.

Sarathi's official instructions say the path for supported states is:

Select State → Learner License → Print Learners License (FORM 3) → Application Number + DOB → Submit. 
Parivahan

Keep the PDF on your phone and preferably print a copy.

Now you can practise legally subject to learner-driver rules. Remember that an LL isn't the final licence.

8. Practise for the driving test

This is where you should spend your time actually learning.

For a car, become comfortable with starting/stopping smoothly, clutch control if manual, steering, reversing, mirrors, indicators, parking, gradients and following road signs.

For a motorcycle, practise balance at low speed, smooth starts/stops, turning, indicators, braking and the manoeuvres expected at your testing track.

Don't just memorise the test track. Get comfortable controlling the vehicle safely.

9. Wait at least 30 days

You cannot immediately take the permanent DL test.

Maharashtra states that after 30 days have passed since obtaining your learner's licence, you can apply for the permanent licence driving test. 
Transport Maharashtra

So, for example:

LL issued 1 August → DL test application eligibility from around 31 August onward.

Don't let the LL expire while putting this off.

10. Apply for the permanent Driving Licence

Return to:

Sarathi Parivahan

Select Maharashtra again.

This time choose the service for New Driving Licence.

Enter your learner's licence/application details and complete the DL application. This corresponds to Form 4, the application for a licence to drive a motor vehicle. 
Transport Maharashtra

Then complete the stages Sarathi gives you:

Application → documents/details → fee payment → driving-test slot booking

Book an available test date at the appropriate RTO.

11. Prepare for your RTO driving test

For the permanent licence stage, you have to demonstrate that you can actually operate the vehicle.

Maharashtra lists the learner's licence, Form 4, applicable documents/photographs and fees among the permanent-licence requirements. It also says the vehicle used for the test must have valid documents. 
Transport Maharashtra

So if you're taking your own/family vehicle, make sure its documents are valid.

Bring the documents shown on your appointment/application acknowledgement rather than relying on a generic checklist, because Sarathi can specify requirements for your particular application.

12. Take the test

At the RTO/testing track, follow the examiner's instructions.

If you're testing for MCWG + LMV, expect to demonstrate the required skills for the relevant vehicle classes.

Don't rush. Use mirrors, indicators and proper observations. A technically completed manoeuvre isn't enough if you're driving unsafely.

If you fail, you don't have to restart the entire licence journey; follow Sarathi/RTO instructions for paying the applicable retest fee and booking another test.

13. After you pass

Once the test is passed and the licensing authority approves the application, your permanent Driving Licence is issued.

You can track it through Sarathi using your application details. Once issued, you can also keep the digital DL available through government-supported services such as mParivahan; the official mParivahan service includes Virtual DL functionality. 
mParivahan

So your complete journey is:

Sarathi → Maharashtra → New Learner's Licence → application → documents → fee → LL test → PASS → download LL → practise → 30+ days → New Driving Licence → pay → book driving test → RTO test → PASS → DL issued.

You absolutely can do this without an agent.

Yep. If you're applying in Maharashtra, you can handle the whole process yourself—no driving school or agent is required for a normal private motorcycle/car licence.

The process is basically:

Learner's Licence (LL) → learn/practise → wait at least 30 days → Driving Licence application → driving test → permanent DL

Maharashtra's official guidance confirms that you can apply for the permanent licence after 30 days from obtaining the learner's licence. 
Transport Maharashtra
+1

1. Decide which vehicle classes you need

If you want a normal bike + car licence, you'll generally be dealing with:

MCWG — Motorcycle With Gear

LMV — Light Motor Vehicle, for private cars

If you intend to drive both, select both classes when the portal offers them rather than unnecessarily doing separate applications.

For ordinary private vehicles, you need to be 18 or older. Maharashtra's official LL page confirms this eligibility. 
Transport Maharashtra

2. Keep your documents ready

Before starting, keep your Aadhaar, proof of age, proof of address, passport-size photos if required, and your mobile phone available. The Maharashtra Motor Vehicle Department lists proof of residence, proof of age, citizenship proof, photographs and the applicable fee among the LL requirements. 
Transport Maharashtra

The online process can differ somewhat depending on whether Aadhaar authentication/faceless services are available for your application, so follow what Sarathi specifically asks you to upload or present.

3. Start on the official Sarathi website

Use the Government of India's official portal:

Sarathi Parivahan

Select Maharashtra.

Once Maharashtra loads, find the option for Learner Licence → Application for New Learner Licence. The exact menu layout can change, so focus on the wording rather than the position of the button.

Do not choose "New Driving Licence" yet. That's the second stage after obtaining your LL.

4. Complete the New Learner's Licence application

You'll be given an application form. Fill in your details exactly as they appear on your official documents, especially your:

Name → DOB → address → Aadhaar/details requested → contact information → vehicle class

For bike + car, choose the appropriate motorcycle class and LMV.

After submission, save your application number. Screenshot it as well.

You'll use that number for payment, appointments, application status and other services.

5. Upload/verify documents and pay the LL fee

Complete whatever stages Sarathi shows for your application, such as document upload, photo/signature, Aadhaar authentication, fee payment and LL test/slot booking.

Maharashtra's current published fee table lists the learner's licence fee as ₹151 per vehicle class plus ₹50 test fee. Your actual payable amount should be taken from the amount Sarathi calculates for your application. 
Transport Maharashtra

Sarathi's payment system allows you to use the application number and DOB to calculate the applicable fee, make payment, verify payment status and print the receipt. 
Sarathi

Save the payment receipt.

6. Take the Learner's Licence test

The LL test is a theory/knowledge test—not the actual car/bike driving test.

Study things such as road signs, traffic signals, right of way, overtaking rules, parking rules, speed/road-safety rules and basic driver responsibilities.

Maharashtra says you need 60% correct answers to pass the preliminary LL test. If you fail, you can book another appointment and retake it. 
Transport Maharashtra

Depending on the workflow offered for your application, the test/verification may be online/faceless or may require an RTO visit.

7. Get your Learner's Licence

After passing and approval, download your LL.

Sarathi's official instructions say the path for supported states is:

Select State → Learner License → Print Learners License (FORM 3) → Application Number + DOB → Submit. 
Parivahan

Keep the PDF on your phone and preferably print a copy.

Now you can practise legally subject to learner-driver rules. Remember that an LL isn't the final licence.

8. Practise for the driving test

This is where you should spend your time actually learning.

For a car, become comfortable with starting/stopping smoothly, clutch control if manual, steering, reversing, mirrors, indicators, parking, gradients and following road signs.

For a motorcycle, practise balance at low speed, smooth starts/stops, turning, indicators, braking and the manoeuvres expected at your testing track.

Don't just memorise the test track. Get comfortable controlling the vehicle safely.

9. Wait at least 30 days

You cannot immediately take the permanent DL test.

Maharashtra states that after 30 days have passed since obtaining your learner's licence, you can apply for the permanent licence driving test. 
Transport Maharashtra

So, for example:

LL issued 1 August → DL test application eligibility from around 31 August onward.

Don't let the LL expire while putting this off.

10. Apply for the permanent Driving Licence

Return to:

Sarathi Parivahan

Select Maharashtra again.

This time choose the service for New Driving Licence.

Enter your learner's licence/application details and complete the DL application. This corresponds to Form 4, the application for a licence to drive a motor vehicle. 
Transport Maharashtra

Then complete the stages Sarathi gives you:

Application → documents/details → fee payment → driving-test slot booking

Book an available test date at the appropriate RTO.

11. Prepare for your RTO driving test

For the permanent licence stage, you have to demonstrate that you can actually operate the vehicle.

Maharashtra lists the learner's licence, Form 4, applicable documents/photographs and fees among the permanent-licence requirements. It also says the vehicle used for the test must have valid documents. 
Transport Maharashtra

So if you're taking your own/family vehicle, make sure its documents are valid.

Bring the documents shown on your appointment/application acknowledgement rather than relying on a generic checklist, because Sarathi can specify requirements for your particular application.

12. Take the test

At the RTO/testing track, follow the examiner's instructions.

If you're testing for MCWG + LMV, expect to demonstrate the required skills for the relevant vehicle classes.

Don't rush. Use mirrors, indicators and proper observations. A technically completed manoeuvre isn't enough if you're driving unsafely.

If you fail, you don't have to restart the entire licence journey; follow Sarathi/RTO instructions for paying the applicable retest fee and booking another test.

13. After you pass

Once the test is passed and the licensing authority approves the application, your permanent Driving Licence is issued.

You can track it through Sarathi using your application details. Once issued, you can also keep the digital DL available through government-supported services such as mParivahan; the official mParivahan service includes Virtual DL functionality. 
mParivahan

So your complete journey is:

Sarathi → Maharashtra → New Learner's Licence → application → documents → fee → LL test → PASS → download LL → practise → 30+ days → New Driving Licence → pay → book driving test → RTO test → PASS → DL issued.

You absolutely can do this without an agent.

 and select Maharashtra. If you send me a screenshot of the page you reach, I can guide you one click at a time from that exact screen, including what to select and what not to select.

Yes. If you're applying for your first driving licence in Maharashtra, the website process has two stages:

Learner's Licence (LL) → wait at least 30 days → Permanent Driving Licence (DL) + driving test. Your LL remains valid for 6 months. 
Parivahan
+1

Part 1 — Apply for your Learner's Licence

Go to the official government portal:

Sarathi Parivahan – Driving Licence Portal

1. Select Maharashtra

You'll see “Select State Name”.

Choose Maharashtra from the dropdown. This opens the Maharashtra Sarathi portal.

2. Start a new Learner's Licence application

On the Maharashtra portal, open:

Learner Licence → Application for New Learner's Licence

The exact wording/layout can vary slightly by state or portal update, but this is the official route specified by Parivahan. 
Parivahan

Read the instructions and press Continue.

3. Choose your applicant category

Because this is your first licence, choose the option indicating that you do not hold an existing Driving/Learner's Licence, if the portal asks.

Do not select an option for an existing DL unless you already have one.

4. Authentication

Sarathi may offer Aadhaar-based authentication depending on the services currently enabled for Maharashtra.

If Aadhaar authentication is offered and your Aadhaar details/mobile are suitable, it's usually the simplest route. Follow the OTP verification shown by Sarathi.

If you use a non-Aadhaar route, additional document verification/RTO steps may be required.

5. Fill in your personal information

Enter the requested information carefully, such as your name, date of birth, gender, parent/guardian details, address, contact information and other fields shown.

Keep spellings consistent with your supporting documents, especially your name, DOB and address.

6. Select your RTO

Choose the RTO applicable to your address/jurisdiction.

Be careful here: Parivahan says the RTO associated with an application can be changed before fee payment, so check it before paying. 
Parivahan

7. Select the vehicle class

This determines what you're getting licensed to drive.

For a normal personal car, you'll generally be looking for LMV (Light Motor Vehicle).

For motorcycles, the portal can show motorcycle categories depending on the type of vehicle/licence being requested.

If you want to drive both a car and motorcycle, make sure the appropriate classes are included in your LL application rather than accidentally applying only for one.

8. Complete the application

Check everything you've entered and submit the application.

Sarathi should generate an Application Number.

Save that number immediately — screenshot it or write it down. You'll use it for payment, application status, LL test and other services.

9. Upload the required documents

Depending on the Maharashtra workflow shown for your application, Sarathi may ask you to upload scanned documents.

Follow:

Upload Documents → Upload/Scan Documents

The exact document requirements shown by Sarathi take priority because services and requirements can vary by state/application. 
Parivahan

You'll generally need documentation establishing things such as age and address, plus any declarations/forms requested by the portal.

Form 1 is the physical-fitness self-declaration. Parivahan states Form 1A medical certificate is required for LL applicants aged 40 or above; other circumstances, such as certain vehicle categories, can also affect requirements, so follow what Sarathi generates for your application. 
Parivahan
+1

10. Photo/signature

Complete the photo and signature step if Sarathi asks you to upload or capture them online.

If the portal instead requires these to be captured/verified at the RTO, follow the instructions generated for your application.

11. Pay the LL fees

Open the fee/payment option for your application.

You'll normally enter your:

Application Number → Date of Birth → Calculate Fee

Then select the available payment method/gateway, complete CAPTCHA if shown and make the payment.

Keep the payment receipt and reference details. Sarathi also provides Verify Pay Status and Print Receipt functions. 
Sarathi Parivahan

12. Complete/Book the Learner's Licence test

The next step is the LL knowledge test, covering things such as road signs, traffic rules and basic driving regulations.

Depending on the services enabled for your application/state, Sarathi may provide an online LL test or require an appointment/visit.

For states/applications supporting the online test, Parivahan's route is:

Learner Licence → Online Learners' License Test (STALL)

Then enter your LL application details, DOB and password as requested. Parivahan notes that online LL testing is only available where the service is enabled. 
Parivahan

If Sarathi instead tells you to book an appointment/visit the RTO, follow that workflow and carry the original documents and fee receipt. The official LL instructions specifically say applicants may need to visit the RTO on the scheduled date with originals and the fee slip. 
Parivahan

13. Pass the LL test

Complete the test.

Once your application/test is approved, your Learner's Licence will be issued.

You can generally retrieve it through:

Learner Licence → Print Learner Licence (Form 3)

Enter your Application Number + DOB and submit. 
Parivahan

Part 2 — Learn and practise driving

Now you have your Learner's Licence.

Your LL is valid for 6 months, and you become eligible to apply for the new Driving Licence after 30 days. 
Parivahan

So use this period to practise the vehicle classes covered by your LL and prepare for the practical test.

Part 3 — Apply for the Permanent Driving Licence

After you've held your LL for at least 30 days, return to:

Sarathi Parivahan

Select Maharashtra again.

14. Choose New Driving Licence

On the Maharashtra portal, go to the Driving Licence section and choose:

New Driving Licence

You'll be asked for your existing:

Yes. If you're applying for your first driving licence in Maharashtra, the website process has two stages:

Learner's Licence (LL) → wait at least 30 days → Permanent Driving Licence (DL) + driving test. Your LL remains valid for 6 months. 
Parivahan
+1

Part 1 — Apply for your Learner's Licence

Go to the official government portal:

Sarathi Parivahan – Driving Licence Portal

1. Select Maharashtra

You'll see “Select State Name”.

Choose Maharashtra from the dropdown. This opens the Maharashtra Sarathi portal.

2. Start a new Learner's Licence application

On the Maharashtra portal, open:

Learner Licence → Application for New Learner's Licence

The exact wording/layout can vary slightly by state or portal update, but this is the official route specified by Parivahan. 
Parivahan

Read the instructions and press Continue.

3. Choose your applicant category

Because this is your first licence, choose the option indicating that you do not hold an existing Driving/Learner's Licence, if the portal asks.

Do not select an option for an existing DL unless you already have one.

4. Authentication

Sarathi may offer Aadhaar-based authentication depending on the services currently enabled for Maharashtra.

If Aadhaar authentication is offered and your Aadhaar details/mobile are suitable, it's usually the simplest route. Follow the OTP verification shown by Sarathi.

If you use a non-Aadhaar route, additional document verification/RTO steps may be required.

5. Fill in your personal information

Enter the requested information carefully, such as your name, date of birth, gender, parent/guardian details, address, contact information and other fields shown.

Keep spellings consistent with your supporting documents, especially your name, DOB and address.

6. Select your RTO

Choose the RTO applicable to your address/jurisdiction.

Be careful here: Parivahan says the RTO associated with an application can be changed before fee payment, so check it before paying. 
Parivahan

7. Select the vehicle class

This determines what you're getting licensed to drive.

For a normal personal car, you'll generally be looking for LMV (Light Motor Vehicle).

For motorcycles, the portal can show motorcycle categories depending on the type of vehicle/licence being requested.

If you want to drive both a car and motorcycle, make sure the appropriate classes are included in your LL application rather than accidentally applying only for one.

8. Complete the application

Check everything you've entered and submit the application.

Sarathi should generate an Application Number.

Save that number immediately — screenshot it or write it down. You'll use it for payment, application status, LL test and other services.

9. Upload the required documents

Depending on the Maharashtra workflow shown for your application, Sarathi may ask you to upload scanned documents.

Follow:

Upload Documents → Upload/Scan Documents

The exact document requirements shown by Sarathi take priority because services and requirements can vary by state/application. 
Parivahan

You'll generally need documentation establishing things such as age and address, plus any declarations/forms requested by the portal.

Form 1 is the physical-fitness self-declaration. Parivahan states Form 1A medical certificate is required for LL applicants aged 40 or above; other circumstances, such as certain vehicle categories, can also affect requirements, so follow what Sarathi generates for your application. 
Parivahan
+1

10. Photo/signature

Complete the photo and signature step if Sarathi asks you to upload or capture them online.

If the portal instead requires these to be captured/verified at the RTO, follow the instructions generated for your application.

11. Pay the LL fees

Open the fee/payment option for your application.

You'll normally enter your:

Application Number → Date of Birth → Calculate Fee

Then select the available payment method/gateway, complete CAPTCHA if shown and make the payment.

Keep the payment receipt and reference details. Sarathi also provides Verify Pay Status and Print Receipt functions. 
Sarathi Parivahan

12. Complete/Book the Learner's Licence test

The next step is the LL knowledge test, covering things such as road signs, traffic rules and basic driving regulations.

Depending on the services enabled for your application/state, Sarathi may provide an online LL test or require an appointment/visit.

For states/applications supporting the online test, Parivahan's route is:

Learner Licence → Online Learners' License Test (STALL)

Then enter your LL application details, DOB and password as requested. Parivahan notes that online LL testing is only available where the service is enabled. 
Parivahan

If Sarathi instead tells you to book an appointment/visit the RTO, follow that workflow and carry the original documents and fee receipt. The official LL instructions specifically say applicants may need to visit the RTO on the scheduled date with originals and the fee slip. 
Parivahan

13. Pass the LL test

Complete the test.

Once your application/test is approved, your Learner's Licence will be issued.

You can generally retrieve it through:

Learner Licence → Print Learner Licence (Form 3)

Enter your Application Number + DOB and submit. 
Parivahan

Part 2 — Learn and practise driving

Now you have your Learner's Licence.

Your LL is valid for 6 months, and you become eligible to apply for the new Driving Licence after 30 days. 
Parivahan

So use this period to practise the vehicle classes covered by your LL and prepare for the practical test.

Part 3 — Apply for the Permanent Driving Licence

After you've held your LL for at least 30 days, return to:

Sarathi Parivahan

Select Maharashtra again.

14. Choose New Driving Licence

On the Maharashtra portal, go to the Driving Licence section and choose:

New Driving Licence

You'll be asked for your existing:

Learner's Licence Number + Date of Birth

Enter them and continue.

Complete the New DL application form. The application corresponds to Form 4 for the permanent driving licence. 
Parivahan

15. Complete the required DL application steps

Check the vehicle class, applicant details and other information pulled from your LL.

Complete any document, declaration, photo/signature or other steps that Sarathi displays for your application.

Then pay the applicable DL/test fees through the portal and keep the receipt.

16. Book your driving test slot

Use the Appointments / DL Test Slot Booking option shown on Sarathi.

Select your RTO, choose an available date/time and confirm the appointment.

Parivahan provides online appointment scheduling for the driving competence test where the facility is available. 
Parivahan

17. Go to the RTO for your driving test

On the scheduled date, go to the relevant RTO with the documents/receipts specified on your acknowledgement.

The practical test is conducted by the competent authority.

You need to demonstrate that you can safely operate the relevant vehicle. Parivahan also says the applicant should bring the type of vehicle corresponding to the application for the test. 
Parivahan

If you're applying for more than one vehicle class, follow the RTO/Sarathi instructions for testing for those classes.

18. Pass the driving test

If you pass, the RTO processes your application for issuance of the Driving Licence.

Parivahan states that after successful completion of the competence test, the DL is issued and sent by Speed Post to the address provided. 
Parivahan

So the entire journey is basically:

Sarathi → Maharashtra → New Learner's Licence → application → documents → photo/signature → fees → LL test → LL issued → wait minimum 30 days → New Driving Licence → fees → book driving test → RTO practical test → pass → DL issued.

Part 1 — Apply for your Learner's Licence

Go to the official government portal:

Sarathi Parivahan – Driving Licence Portal

1. Select Maharashtra

You'll see “Select State Name”.

Choose Maharashtra from the dropdown. This opens the Maharashtra Sarathi portal.

2. Start a new Learner's Licence application

On the Maharashtra portal, open:

Learner Licence → Application for New Learner's Licence

The exact wording/layout can vary slightly by state or portal update, but this is the official route specified by Parivahan. 
Parivahan

Read the instructions and press Continue.

3. Choose your applicant category

Because this is your first licence, choose the option indicating that you do not hold an existing Driving/Learner's Licence, if the portal asks.

Do not select an option for an existing DL unless you already have one.

4. Authentication

Sarathi may offer Aadhaar-based authentication depending on the services currently enabled for Maharashtra.

If Aadhaar authentication is offered and your Aadhaar details/mobile are suitable, it's usually the simplest route. Follow the OTP verification shown by Sarathi.

If you use a non-Aadhaar route, additional document verification/RTO steps may be required.

5. Fill in your personal information

Enter the requested information carefully, such as your name, date of birth, gender, parent/guardian details, address, contact information and other fields shown.

Keep spellings consistent with your supporting documents, especially your name, DOB and address.

6. Select your RTO

Choose the RTO applicable to your address/jurisdiction.

Be careful here: Parivahan says the RTO associated with an application can be changed before fee payment, so check it before paying. 
Parivahan

7. Select the vehicle class

This determines what you're getting licensed to drive.

For a normal personal car, you'll generally be looking for LMV (Light Motor Vehicle).

For motorcycles, the portal can show motorcycle categories depending on the type of vehicle/licence being requested.

If you want to drive both a car and motorcycle, make sure the appropriate classes are included in your LL application rather than accidentally applying only for one.

8. Complete the application

Check everything you've entered and submit the application.

Sarathi should generate an Application Number.

Save that number immediately — screenshot it or write it down. You'll use it for payment, application status, LL test and other services.

9. Upload the required documents

Depending on the Maharashtra workflow shown for your application, Sarathi may ask you to upload scanned documents.

Follow:

Upload Documents → Upload/Scan Documents

The exact document requirements shown by Sarathi take priority because services and requirements can vary by state/application. 
Parivahan

You'll generally need documentation establishing things such as age and address, plus any declarations/forms requested by the portal.

Form 1 is the physical-fitness self-declaration. Parivahan states Form 1A medical certificate is required for LL applicants aged 40 or above; other circumstances, such as certain vehicle categories, can also affect requirements, so follow what Sarathi generates for your application.

10. Photo/signature

Complete the photo and signature step if Sarathi asks you to upload or capture them online.

If the portal instead requires these to be captured/verified at the RTO, follow the instructions generated for your application.

11. Pay the LL fees

Open the fee/payment option for your application.

You'll normally enter your:

Application Number → Date of Birth → Calculate Fee

Then select the available payment method/gateway, complete CAPTCHA if shown and make the payment.

Keep the payment receipt and reference details. Sarathi also provides Verify Pay Status and Print Receipt functions. 
Sarathi Parivahan

12. Complete/Book the Learner's Licence test

The next step is the LL knowledge test, covering things such as road signs, traffic rules and basic driving regulations.

Depending on the services enabled for your application/state, Sarathi may provide an online LL test or require an appointment/visit.

For states/applications supporting the online test, Parivahan's route is:

Learner Licence → Online Learners' License Test (STALL)

Then enter your LL application details, DOB and password as requested. Parivahan notes that online LL testing is only available where the service is enabled. 
Parivahan

If Sarathi instead tells you to book an appointment/visit the RTO, follow that workflow and carry the original documents and fee receipt. The official LL instructions specifically say applicants may need to visit the RTO on the scheduled date with originals and the fee slip. 
Parivahan

13. Pass the LL test

Complete the test.

Once your application/test is approved, your Learner's Licence will be issued.

You can generally retrieve it through:

Learner Licence → Print Learner Licence (Form 3)

Enter your Application Number + DOB and submit. 
Parivahan

Part 2 — Learn and practise driving

Now you have your Learner's Licence.

Your LL is valid for 6 months, and you become eligible to apply for the new Driving Licence after 30 days. 
Parivahan

So use this period to practise the vehicle classes covered by your LL and prepare for the practical test.

Part 3 — Apply for the Permanent Driving Licence

After you've held your LL for at least 30 days, return to:

Sarathi Parivahan

Select Maharashtra again.

14. Choose New Driving Licence

On the Maharashtra portal, go to the Driving Licence section and choose:

New Driving Licence

You'll be asked for your existing:

Learner's Licence Number + Date of Birth

Enter them and continue.

Complete the New DL application form. The application corresponds to Form 4 for the permanent driving licence. 
Parivahan

15. Complete the required DL application steps

Check the vehicle class, applicant details and other information pulled from your LL.

Complete any document, declaration, photo/signature or other steps that Sarathi displays for your application.

Then pay the applicable DL/test fees through the portal and keep the receipt.

16. Book your driving test slot

Use the Appointments / DL Test Slot Booking option shown on Sarathi.

Select your RTO, choose an available date/time and confirm the appointment.

Parivahan provides online appointment scheduling for the driving competence test where the facility is available. 
Parivahan

17. Go to the RTO for your driving test

On the scheduled date, go to the relevant RTO with the documents/receipts specified on your acknowledgement.

The practical test is conducted by the competent authority.

You need to demonstrate that you can safely operate the relevant vehicle. Parivahan also says the applicant should bring the type of vehicle corresponding to the application for the test. 
Parivahan

If you're applying for more than one vehicle class, follow the RTO/Sarathi instructions for testing for those classes.

18. Pass the driving test

If you pass, the RTO processes your application for issuance of the Driving Licence.

Parivahan states that after successful completion of the competence test, the DL is issued and sent by Speed Post to the address provided. 
Parivahan

So the entire journey is basically:

Sarathi → Maharashtra → New Learner's Licence → application → documents → photo/signature → fees → LL test → LL issued → wait minimum 30 days → New Driving Licence → fees → book driving test → RTO practical test → pass → DL issued.

Yes. If you're applying for your first driving licence in Maharashtra, the website process has two stages:

Learner's Licence (LL) → wait at least 30 days → Permanent Driving Licence (DL) + driving test. Your LL remains valid for 6 months. 
Parivahan
+1

Part 1 — Apply for your Learner's Licence

Go to the official government portal:

Sarathi Parivahan – Driving Licence Portal

1. Select Maharashtra

You'll see “Select State Name”.

Choose Maharashtra from the dropdown. This opens the Maharashtra Sarathi portal.

2. Start a new Learner's Licence application

On the Maharashtra portal, open:

Learner Licence → Application for New Learner's Licence

The exact wording/layout can vary slightly by state or portal update, but this is the official route specified by Parivahan. 
Parivahan

Read the instructions and press Continue.

3. Choose your applicant category

Because this is your first licence, choose the option indicating that you do not hold an existing Driving/Learner's Licence, if the portal asks.

Do not select an option for an existing DL unless you already have one.

4. Authentication

Sarathi may offer Aadhaar-based authentication depending on the services currently enabled for Maharashtra.

If Aadhaar authentication is offered and your Aadhaar details/mobile are suitable, it's usually the simplest route. Follow the OTP verification shown by Sarathi.

If you use a non-Aadhaar route, additional document verification/RTO steps may be required.

5. Fill in your personal information

Enter the requested information carefully, such as your name, date of birth, gender, parent/guardian details, address, contact information and other fields shown.

Keep spellings consistent with your supporting documents, especially your name, DOB and address.

6. Select your RTO

Choose the RTO applicable to your address/jurisdiction.

Be careful here: Parivahan says the RTO associated with an application can be changed before fee payment, so check it before paying. 
Parivahan

7. Select the vehicle class

This determines what you're getting licensed to drive.

For a normal personal car, you'll generally be looking for LMV (Light Motor Vehicle).

For motorcycles, the portal can show motorcycle categories depending on the type of vehicle/licence being requested.

If you want to drive both a car and motorcycle, make sure the appropriate classes are included in your LL application rather than accidentally applying only for one.

8. Complete the application

Check everything you've entered and submit the application.

Sarathi should generate an Application Number.

Save that number immediately — screenshot it or write it down. You'll use it for payment, application status, LL test and other services.

9. Upload the required documents

Depending on the Maharashtra workflow shown for your application, Sarathi may ask you to upload scanned documents.

Follow:

Upload Documents → Upload/Scan Documents

The exact document requirements shown by Sarathi take priority because services and requirements can vary by state/application. 
Parivahan

You'll generally need documentation establishing things such as age and address, plus any declarations/forms requested by the portal.

Form 1 is the physical-fitness self-declaration. Parivahan states Form 1A medical certificate is required for LL applicants aged 40 or above; other circumstances, such as certain vehicle categories, can also affect requirements, so follow what Sarathi generates for your application.

Open the fee/payment option for your application.

You'll normally enter your:

Application Number → Date of Birth → Calculate Fee

Then select the available payment method/gateway, complete CAPTCHA if shown and make the payment.

Keep the payment receipt and reference details. Sarathi also provides Verify Pay Status and Print Receipt functions. 
Sarathi Parivahan

12. Complete/Book the Learner's Licence test

The next step is the LL knowledge test, covering things such as road signs, traffic rules and basic driving regulations.

Depending on the services enabled for your application/state, Sarathi may provide an online LL test or require an appointment/visit.

For states/applications supporting the online test, Parivahan's route is:

Learner Licence → Online Learners' License Test (STALL)

Then enter your LL application details, DOB and password as requested. Parivahan notes that online LL testing is only available where the service is enabled. 
Parivahan

If Sarathi instead tells you to book an appointment/visit the RTO, follow that workflow and carry the original documents and fee receipt. The official LL instructions specifically say applicants may need to visit the RTO on the scheduled date with originals and the fee slip. 
Parivahan

13. Pass the LL test

Complete the test.

Once your application/test is approved, your Learner's Licence will be issued.

You can generally retrieve it through:

Learner Licence → Print Learner Licence (Form 3)

Enter your Application Number + DOB and submit. 
Parivahan

Part 2 — Learn and practise driving

Now you have your Learner's Licence.

Your LL is valid for 6 months, and you become eligible to apply for the new Driving Licence after 30 days. 
Parivahan

So use this period to practise the vehicle classes covered by your LL and prepare for the practical test.

Part 3 — Apply for the Permanent Driving Licence

After you've held your LL for at least 30 days, return to:

Sarathi Parivahan

Select Maharashtra again.

14. Choose New Driving Licence

On the Maharashtra portal, go to the Driving Licence section and choose:

New Driving Licence

You'll be asked for your existing:

Learner's Licence Number + Date of Birth

Enter them and continue.

Complete the New DL application form. The application corresponds to Form 4 for the permanent driving licence. 
Parivahan

15. Complete the required DL application steps

Check the vehicle class, applicant details and other information pulled from your LL.

Complete any document, declaration, photo/signature or other steps that Sarathi displays for your application.

Then pay the applicable DL/test fees through the portal and keep the receipt.

16. Book your driving test slot

Use the Appointments / DL Test Slot Booking option shown on Sarathi.

Select your RTO, choose an available date/time and confirm the appointment.

Parivahan provides online appointment scheduling for the driving competence test where the facility is available. 
Parivahan

On the scheduled date, go to the relevant RTO with the documents/receipts specified on your acknowledgement.

The practical test is conducted by the competent authority.

You need to demonstrate that you can safely operate the relevant vehicle. Parivahan also says the applicant should bring the type of vehicle corresponding to the application for the test. 
Parivahan

If you're applying for more than one vehicle class, follow the RTO/Sarathi instructions for testing for those classes.

18. Pass the driving test

If you pass, the RTO processes your application for issuance of the Driving Licence.

Parivahan states that after successful completion of the competence test, the DL is issued and sent by Speed Post to the address provided. 
Parivahan

Yes. If you're applying for your first driving licence in Maharashtra, the website process has two stages:

Learner's Licence (LL) → wait at least 30 days → Permanent Driving Licence (DL) + driving test. Your LL remains valid for 6 months. 
Parivahan
+1

Part 1 — Apply for your Learner's Licence

Go to the official government portal:

Sarathi Parivahan – Driving Licence Portal

1. Select Maharashtra

You'll see “Select State Name”.

Choose Maharashtra from the dropdown. This opens the Maharashtra Sarathi portal.

2. Start a new Learner's Licence application

On the Maharashtra portal, open:

Learner Licence → Application for New Learner's Licence

The exact wording/layout can vary slightly by state or portal update, but this is the official route specified by Parivahan. 
Parivahan

Read the instructions and press Continue.

3. Choose your applicant category

Because this is your first licence, choose the option indicating that you do not hold an existing Driving/Learner's Licence, if the portal asks.

Do not select an option for an existing DL unless you already have one.

4. Authentication

Sarathi may offer Aadhaar-based authentication depending on the services currently enabled for Maharashtra.

If Aadhaar authentication is offered and your Aadhaar details/mobile are suitable, it's usually the simplest route. Follow the OTP verification shown by Sarathi.

If you use a non-Aadhaar route, additional document verification/RTO steps may be required.

5. Fill in your personal information

Enter the requested information carefully, such as your name, date of birth, gender, parent/guardian details, address, contact information and other fields shown.

Keep spellings consistent with your supporting documents, especially your name, DOB and address.

6. Select your RTO

Choose the RTO applicable to your address/jurisdiction.

Be careful here: Parivahan says the RTO associated with an application can be changed before fee payment, so check it before paying. 
Parivahan

7. Select the vehicle class

This determines what you're getting licensed to drive.

For a normal personal car, you'll generally be looking for LMV (Light Motor Vehicle).

For motorcycles, the portal can show motorcycle categories depending on the type of vehicle/licence being requested.

If you want to drive both a car and motorcycle, make sure the appropriate classes are included in your LL application rather than accidentally applying only for one.

8. Complete the application

Check everything you've entered and submit the application.

Sarathi should generate an Application Number.

Save that number immediately — screenshot it or write it down. You'll use it for payment, application status, LL test and other services.

9. Upload the required documents

Depending on the Maharashtra workflow shown for your application, Sarathi may ask you to upload scanned documents.

Follow:

Upload Documents → Upload/Scan Documents

The exact document requirements shown by Sarathi take priority because services and requirements can vary by state/application. 
Parivahan

You'll generally need documentation establishing things such as age and address, plus any declarations/forms requested by the portal.

Form 1 is the physical-fitness self-declaration. Parivahan states Form 1A medical certificate is required for LL applicants aged 40 or above; other circumstances, such as certain vehicle categories, can also affect requirements, so follow what Sarathi generates for your application. 
Parivahan
+1

10. Photo/signature

Complete the photo and signature step if Sarathi asks you to upload or capture them online.

If the portal instead requires these to be captured/verified at the RTO, follow the instructions generated for your application.

11. Pay the LL fees

Open the fee/payment option for your application.

You'll normally enter your:

Application Number → Date of Birth → Calculate Fee

Then select the available payment method/gateway, complete CAPTCHA if shown and make the payment.

Keep the payment receipt and reference details. Sarathi also provides Verify Pay Status and Print Receipt functions. 
Sarathi Parivahan

12. Complete/Book the Learner's Licence test

The next step is the LL knowledge test, covering things such as road signs, traffic rules and basic driving regulations.

Depending on the services enabled for your application/state, Sarathi may provide an online LL test or require an appointment/visit.

For states/applications supporting the online test, Parivahan's route is:

Learner Licence → Online Learners' License Test (STALL)

Then enter your LL application details, DOB and password as requested. Parivahan notes that online LL testing is only available where the service is enabled. 
Parivahan

If Sarathi instead tells you to book an appointment/visit the RTO, follow that workflow and carry the original documents and fee receipt. The official LL instructions specifically say applicants may need to visit the RTO on the scheduled date with originals and the fee slip. 
Parivahan

13. Pass the LL test

Complete the test.

Once your application/test is approved, your Learner's Licence will be issued.

You can generally retrieve it through:

Learner Licence → Print Learner Licence (Form 3)

Enter your Application Number + DOB and submit. 
Parivahan

Part 2 — Learn and practise driving

Now you have your Learner's Licence.

Your LL is valid for 6 months, and you become eligible to apply for the new Driving Licence after 30 days. 
Parivahan

So use this period to practise the vehicle classes covered by your LL and prepare for the practical test.

Part 3 — Apply for the Permanent Driving Licence

After you've held your LL for at least 30 days, return to:

Sarathi Parivahan

Select Maharashtra again.

14. Choose New Driving Licence

On the Maharashtra portal, go to the Driving Licence section and choose:

New Driving Licence

You'll be asked for your existing:

Learner's Licence Number + Date of Birth

Enter them and continue.

Complete the New DL application form. The application corresponds to Form 4 for the permanent driving licence. 
Parivahan

15. Complete the required DL application steps

Check the vehicle class, applicant details and other information pulled from your LL.

Complete any document, declaration, photo/signature or other steps that Sarathi displays for your application.

Then pay the applicable DL/test fees through the portal and keep the receipt.

16. Book your driving test slot

Use the Appointments / DL Test Slot Booking option shown on Sarathi.

Select your RTO, choose an available date/time and confirm the appointment.

Parivahan provides online appointment scheduling for the driving competence test where the facility is available. 
Parivahan

17. Go to the RTO for your driving test

On the scheduled date, go to the relevant RTO with the documents/receipts specified on your acknowledgement.

The practical test is conducted by the competent authority.

You need to demonstrate that you can safely operate the relevant vehicle. Parivahan also says the applicant should bring the type of vehicle corresponding to the application for the test. 
Parivahan

If you're applying for more than one vehicle class, follow the RTO/Sarathi instructions for testing for those classes.

18. Pass the driving test

If you pass, the RTO processes your application for issuance of the Driving Licence.

Parivahan states that after successful completion of the competence test, the DL is issued and sent by Speed Post to the address provided. 
Parivahan

So the entire journey is basically:

Sarathi → Maharashtra → New Learner's Licence → application → documents → photo/signature → fees → LL test → LL issued → wait minimum 30 days → New Driving Licence → fees → book driving test → RTO practical test → pass → DL issued.

Yes. If you're applying for your first driving licence in Maharashtra, the website process has two stages:

Learner's Licence (LL) → wait at least 30 days → Permanent Driving Licence (DL) + driving test. Your LL remains valid for 6 months. 
Parivahan
+1

Part 1 — Apply for your Learner's Licence

Go to the official government portal:

Sarathi Parivahan – Driving Licence Portal

1. Select Maharashtra

You'll see “Select State Name”.

Choose Maharashtra from the dropdown. This opens the Maharashtra Sarathi portal.

2. Start a new Learner's Licence application

On the Maharashtra portal, open:

Learner Licence → Application for New Learner's Licence

The exact wording/layout can vary slightly by state or portal update, but this is the official route specified by Parivahan. 
Parivahan

Read the instructions and press Continue.

3. Choose your applicant category

Because this is your first licence, choose the option indicating that you do not hold an existing Driving/Learner's Licence, if the portal asks.

Do not select an option for an existing DL unless you already have one.

4. Authentication

Sarathi may offer Aadhaar-based authentication depending on the services currently enabled for Maharashtra.

If Aadhaar authentication is offered and your Aadhaar details/mobile are suitable, it's usually the simplest route. Follow the OTP verification shown by Sarathi.

If you use a non-Aadhaar route, additional document verification/RTO steps may be required.

5. Fill in your personal information

Enter the requested information carefully, such as your name, date of birth, gender, parent/guardian details, address, contact information and other fields shown.

Keep spellings consistent with your supporting documents, especially your name, DOB and address.

6. Select your RTO

Choose the RTO applicable to your address/jurisdiction.

Be careful here: Parivahan says the RTO associated with an application can be changed before fee payment, so check it before paying. 
Parivahan

7. Select the vehicle class

This determines what you're getting licensed to drive.

For a normal personal car, you'll generally be looking for LMV (Light Motor Vehicle).

For motorcycles, the portal can show motorcycle categories depending on the type of vehicle/licence being requested.

If you want to drive both a car and motorcycle, make sure the appropriate classes are included in your LL application rather than accidentally applying only for one.

8. Complete the application

Check everything you've entered and submit the application.

Sarathi should generate an Application Number.

Save that number immediately — screenshot it or write it down. You'll use it for payment, application status, LL test and other services.

9. Upload the required documents

Depending on the Maharashtra workflow shown for your application, Sarathi may ask you to upload scanned documents.

Follow:

Upload Documents → Upload/Scan Documents

The exact document requirements shown by Sarathi take priority because services and requirements can vary by state/application. 
Parivahan

You'll generally need documentation establishing things such as age and address, plus any declarations/forms requested by the portal.

Form 1 is the physical-fitness self-declaration. Parivahan states Form 1A medical certificate is required for LL applicants aged 40 or above; other circumstances, such as certain vehicle categories, can also affect requirements, so follow what Sarathi generates for your application. 
Parivahan
+1

10. Photo/signature

Complete the photo and signature step if Sarathi asks you to upload or capture them online.

If the portal instead requires these to be captured/verified at the RTO, follow the instructions generated for your application.

11. Pay the LL fees

Open the fee/payment option for your application.

You'll normally enter your:

Application Number → Date of Birth → Calculate Fee

Then select the available payment method/gateway, complete CAPTCHA if shown and make the payment.

Keep the payment receipt and reference details. Sarathi also provides Verify Pay Status and Print Receipt functions. 
Sarathi Parivahan

12. Complete/Book the Learner's Licence test

The next step is the LL knowledge test, covering things such as road signs, traffic rules and basic driving regulations.

Depending on the services enabled for your application/state, Sarathi may provide an online LL test or require an appointment/visit.

For states/applications supporting the online test, Parivahan's route is:

Learner Licence → Online Learners' License Test (STALL)

Then enter your LL application details, DOB and password as requested. Parivahan notes that online LL testing is only available where the service is enabled. 
Parivahan

If Sarathi instead tells you to book an appointment/visit the RTO, follow that workflow and carry the original documents and fee receipt. The official LL instructions specifically say applicants may need to visit the RTO on the scheduled date with originals and the fee slip. 
Parivahan

13. Pass the LL test

Complete the test.

Once your application/test is approved, your Learner's Licence will be issued.

You can generally retrieve it through:

Learner Licence → Print Learner Licence (Form 3)

Enter your Application Number + DOB and submit. 
Parivahan

Part 2 — Learn and practise driving

Now you have your Learner's Licence.

Your LL is valid for 6 months, and you become eligible to apply for the new Driving Licence after 30 days. 
Parivahan

So use this period to practise the vehicle classes covered by your LL and prepare for the practical test.

Part 3 — Apply for the Permanent Driving Licence

After you've held your LL for at least 30 days, return to:

Sarathi Parivahan

Select Maharashtra again.

14. Choose New Driving Licence

On the Maharashtra portal, go to the Driving Licence section and choose:

New Driving Licence

You'll be asked for your existing:

Learner's Licence Number + Date of Birth

Enter them and continue.

Complete the New DL application form. The application corresponds to Form 4 for the permanent driving licence. 
Parivahan

15. Complete the required DL application steps

Check the vehicle class, applicant details and other information pulled from your LL.

Complete any document, declaration, photo/signature or other steps that Sarathi displays for your application.

Then pay the applicable DL/test fees through the portal and keep the receipt.

16. Book your driving test slot

Use the Appointments / DL Test Slot Booking option shown on Sarathi.

Select your RTO, choose an available date/time and confirm the appointment.

Parivahan provides online appointment scheduling for the driving competence test where the facility is available. 
Parivahan

17. Go to the RTO for your driving test

On the scheduled date, go to the relevant RTO with the documents/receipts specified on your acknowledgement.

The practical test is conducted by the competent authority.

You need to demonstrate that you can safely operate the relevant vehicle. Parivahan also says the applicant should bring the type of vehicle corresponding to the application for the test. 
Parivahan

If you're applying for more than one vehicle class, follow the RTO/Sarathi instructions for testing for those classes.

18. Pass the driving test

If you pass, the RTO processes your application for issuance of the Driving Licence.

Parivahan states that after successful completion of the competence test, the DL is issued and sent by Speed Post to the address provided. 
Parivahan

So the entire journey is basically:

Sarathi → Maharashtra → New Learner's Licence → application → documents → photo/signature → fees → LL test → LL issued → wait minimum 30 days → New Driving Licence → fees → book driving test → RTO practical test → pass → DL issued.

Sarathi Parivahan — Driving Licence Services

Select → Maharashtra

Step 3 — Start the Learner's Licence application

give me full process 

Yes. If you're applying for your first driving licence in Maharashtra, the website process has two stages:

Learner's Licence (LL) → wait at least 30 days → Permanent Driving Licence (DL) + driving test. Your LL remains valid for 6 months. 
Parivahan
+1

Part 1 — Apply for your Learner's Licence

Go to the official government portal:

Sarathi Parivahan – Driving Licence Portal

1. Select Maharashtra

You'll see “Select State Name”.

Choose Maharashtra from the dropdown. This opens the Maharashtra Sarathi portal.

2. Start a new Learner's Licence application

On the Maharashtra portal, open:

Learner Licence → Application for New Learner's Licence

The exact wording/layout can vary slightly by state or portal update, but this is the official route specified by Parivahan. 
Parivahan

Read the instructions and press Continue.

3. Choose your applicant category

Because this is your first licence, choose the option indicating that you do not hold an existing Driving/Learner's Licence, if the portal asks.

Do not select an option for an existing DL unless you already have one.

4. Authentication

Sarathi may offer Aadhaar-based authentication depending on the services currently enabled for Maharashtra.

If Aadhaar authentication is offered and your Aadhaar details/mobile are suitable, it's usually the simplest route. Follow the OTP verification shown by Sarathi.

If you use a non-Aadhaar route, additional document verification/RTO steps may be required.

5. Fill in your personal information

Enter the requested information carefully, such as your name, date of birth, gender, parent/guardian details, address, contact information and other fields shown.

Keep spellings consistent with your supporting documents, especially your name, DOB and address.

6. Select your RTO

Choose the RTO applicable to your address/jurisdiction.

Be careful here: Parivahan says the RTO associated with an application can be changed before fee payment, so check it before paying. 
Parivahan

7. Select the vehicle class

This determines what you're getting licensed to drive.

For a normal personal car, you'll generally be looking for LMV (Light Motor Vehicle).

For motorcycles, the portal can show motorcycle categories depending on the type of vehicle/licence being requested.

If you want to drive both a car and motorcycle, make sure the appropriate classes are included in your LL application rather than accidentally applying only for one.

8. Complete the application

Check everything you've entered and submit the application.

Sarathi should generate an Application Number.

Save that number immediately — screenshot it or write it down. You'll use it for payment, application status, LL test and other services.

9. Upload the required documents

Depending on the Maharashtra workflow shown for your application, Sarathi may ask you to upload scanned documents.

Follow:

Upload Documents → Upload/Scan Documents

The exact document requirements shown by Sarathi take priority because services and requirements can vary by state/application. 
Parivahan

You'll generally need documentation establishing things such as age and address, plus any declarations/forms requested by the portal.

Form 1 is the physical-fitness self-declaration. Parivahan states Form 1A medical certificate is required for LL applicants aged 40 or above; other circumstances, such as certain vehicle categories, can also affect requirements, so follow what Sarathi generates for your application. 
Parivahan
+1

10. Photo/signature

Complete the photo and signature step if Sarathi asks you to upload or capture them online.

If the portal instead requires these to be captured/verified at the RTO, follow the instructions generated for your application.

11. Pay the LL fees

Open the fee/payment option for your application.

You'll normally enter your:

Application Number → Date of Birth → Calculate Fee

Then select the available payment method/gateway, complete CAPTCHA if shown and make the payment.

Keep the payment receipt and reference details. Sarathi also provides Verify Pay Status and Print Receipt functions. 
Sarathi Parivahan

12. Complete/Book the Learner's Licence test

The next step is the LL knowledge test, covering things such as road signs, traffic rules and basic driving regulations.

Depending on the services enabled for your application/state, Sarathi may provide an online LL test or require an appointment/visit.

For states/applications supporting the online test, Parivahan's route is:

Learner Licence → Online Learners' License Test (STALL)

Then enter your LL application details, DOB and password as requested. Parivahan notes that online LL testing is only available where the service is enabled. 
Parivahan

If Sarathi instead tells you to book an appointment/visit the RTO, follow that workflow and carry the original documents and fee receipt. The official LL instructions specifically say applicants may need to visit the RTO on the scheduled date with originals and the fee slip. 
Parivahan

13. Pass the LL test

Complete the test.

Once your application/test is approved, your Learner's Licence will be issued.

You can generally retrieve it through:

Learner Licence → Print Learner Licence (Form 3)

Enter your Application Number + DOB and submit. 
Parivahan

Part 2 — Learn and practise driving

Now you have your Learner's Licence.

Your LL is valid for 6 months, and you become eligible to apply for the new Driving Licence after 30 days. 
Parivahan

So use this period to practise the vehicle classes covered by your LL and prepare for the practical test.

Part 3 — Apply for the Permanent Driving Licence

After you've held your LL for at least 30 days, return to:

Sarathi Parivahan

Select Maharashtra again.

14. Choose New Driving Licence

On the Maharashtra portal, go to the Driving Licence section and choose:

New Driving Licence

You'll be asked for your existing:

Learner's Licence Number + Date of Birth

Enter them and continue.

Complete the New DL application form. The application corresponds to Form 4 for the permanent driving licence. 
Parivahan

15. Complete the required DL application steps

Check the vehicle class, applicant details and other information pulled from your LL.

Complete any document, declaration, photo/signature or other steps that Sarathi displays for your application.

Then pay the applicable DL/test fees through the portal and keep the receipt.

16. Book your driving test slot

Use the Appointments / DL Test Slot Booking option shown on Sarathi.

Select your RTO, choose an available date/time and confirm the appointment.

Parivahan provides online appointment scheduling for the driving competence test where the facility is available. 
Parivahan

17. Go to the RTO for your driving test

On the scheduled date, go to the relevant RTO with the documents/receipts specified on your acknowledgement.

The practical test is conducted by the competent authority.

You need to demonstrate that you can safely operate the relevant vehicle. Parivahan also says the applicant should bring the type of vehicle corresponding to the application for the test. 
Parivahan

If you're applying for more than one vehicle class, follow the RTO/Sarathi instructions for testing for those classes.

18. Pass the driving test

If you pass, the RTO processes your application for issuance of the Driving Licence.

Parivahan states that after successful completion of the competence test, the DL is issued and sent by Speed Post to the address provided. 
Parivahan

So the entire journey is basically:

Sarathi → Maharashtra → New Learner's Licence → application → documents → photo/signature → fees → LL test → LL issued → wait minimum 30 days → New Driving Licence → fees → book driving test → RTO practical test → pass → DL issued.

Think step-by-step. Parse the intent, form a hypothesis, and delegate to the correct orchestrator rather than executing actions directly yourself."},{"role":"user","content":"Task: Guide me on how to apply for a driver's license on the website 

Yep. If this is your first licence, you start with a Learner's Licence (LL) on Sarathi, then after holding it for at least 30 days, apply for the permanent Driving Licence and driving test. 
Parivahan
+1

Step 1 — Open the official Sarathi website

Sarathi Parivahan — Driving Licence Services

This is the Government of India's official portal. Don't use an agent or random third-party DL website.

Step 2 — Select your state

On the Select State Name screen:

Select → Maharashtra

The Maharashtra Sarathi portal should then open.

Step 3 — Start the Learner's Licence application

On the Maharashtra page, look at the top menu/navigation.

Choose:

Learner Licence → Application for New Learner's Licence

Depending on the current version of the portal, the wording may instead be Apply for New Learner Licence or similar. The official Parivahan instructions confirm the flow is State → Learner's Licence → New Learner's Licence application. 
Parivahan

Step 4 — Follow the application

You'll then go through the LL application process: enter your details, choose the vehicle class you want (for example, motorcycle with gear and/or LMV for a car), complete the required document/photo steps shown for Maharashtra, pay the applicable fee, and complete the LL test/appointment process offered by the portal.

Save your Application Number when Sarathi generates it. You'll need it later for things like application status, payment, and downloading the LL. 
Parivahan
+1

Once your Learner's Licence is issued, you can move on to the permanent DL stage after the required period. Parivahan says you need to have held a valid LL for at least 30 days before taking the driving competence test. 
Parivahan

We can do this screen-by-screen instead of me dumping the whole process on you. Open the Sarathi link above, select Maharashtra, and send me a screenshot of the page you reach. I'll tell you exactly what to click next.

Sources
give me full process 

Yes. If you're applying for your first driving licence in Maharashtra, the website process has two stages:

Learner's Licence (LL) → wait at least 30 days → Permanent Driving Licence (DL) + driving test. Your LL remains valid for 6 months. 
Parivahan
+1

Part 1 — Apply for your Learner's Licence

Go to the official government portal:

Sarathi Parivahan – Driving Licence Portal

1. Select Maharashtra

You'll see “Select State Name”.

Choose Maharashtra from the dropdown. This opens the Maharashtra Sarathi portal.

2. Start a new Learner's Licence application

On the Maharashtra portal, open:

Learner Licence → Application for New Learner's Licence

The exact wording/layout can vary slightly by state or portal update, but this is the official route specified by Parivahan. 
Parivahan

Read the instructions and press Continue.

3. Choose your applicant category

Because this is your first licence, choose the option indicating that you do not hold an existing Driving/Learner's Licence, if the portal asks.

Do not select an option for an existing DL unless you already have one.

4. Authentication

Sarathi may offer Aadhaar-based authentication depending on the services currently enabled for Maharashtra.

If Aadhaar authentication is offered and your Aadhaar details/mobile are suitable, it's usually the simplest route. Follow the OTP verification shown by Sarathi.

If you use a non-Aadhaar route, additional document verification/RTO steps may be required.

5. Fill in your personal information

Enter the requested information carefully, such as your name, date of birth, gender, parent/guardian details, address, contact information and other fields shown.

Keep spellings consistent with your supporting documents, especially your name, DOB and address.

6. Select your RTO

Choose the RTO applicable to your address/jurisdiction.

Be careful here: Parivahan says the RTO associated with an application can be changed before fee payment, so check it before paying. 
Parivahan

7. Select the vehicle class

This determines what you're getting licensed to drive.

For a normal personal car, you'll generally be looking for LMV (Light Motor Vehicle).

For motorcycles, the portal can show motorcycle categories depending on the type of vehicle/licence being requested.

If you want to drive both a car and motorcycle, make sure the appropriate classes are included in your LL application rather than accidentally applying only for one.

8. Complete the application

Check everything you've entered and submit the application.

Sarathi should generate an Application Number.

Save that number immediately — screenshot it or write it down. You'll use it for payment, application status, LL test and other services.

9. Upload the required documents

Depending on the Maharashtra workflow shown for your application, Sarathi may ask you to upload scanned documents.

Follow:

Upload Documents → Upload/Scan Documents

The exact document requirements shown by Sarathi take priority because services and requirements can vary by state/application. 
Parivahan

You'll generally need documentation establishing things such as age and address, plus any declarations/forms requested by the portal.

Form 1 is the physical-fitness self-declaration. Parivahan states Form 1A medical certificate is required for LL applicants aged 40 or above; other circumstances, such as certain vehicle categories, can also affect requirements, so follow what Sarathi generates for your application. 
Parivahan
+1

10. Photo/signature

Complete the photo and signature step if Sarathi asks you to upload or capture them online.

If the portal instead requires these to be captured/verified at the RTO, follow the instructions generated for your application.

11. Pay the LL fees

Open the fee/payment option for your application.

You'll normally enter your:

Application Number → Date of Birth → Calculate Fee

Then select the available payment method/gateway, complete CAPTCHA if shown and make the payment.

Keep the payment receipt and reference details. Sarathi also provides Verify Pay Status and Print Receipt functions. 
Sarathi Parivahan

12. Complete/Book the Learner's Licence test

The next step is the LL knowledge test, covering things such as road signs, traffic rules and basic driving regulations.

Depending on the services enabled for your application/state, Sarathi may provide an online LL test or require an appointment/visit.

For states/applications supporting the online test, Parivahan's route is:

Learner Licence → Online Learners' License Test (STALL)

Then enter your LL application details, DOB and password as requested. Parivahan notes that online LL testing is only available where the service is enabled. 
Parivahan

If Sarathi instead tells you to book an appointment/visit the RTO, follow that workflow and carry the original documents and fee receipt. The official LL instructions specifically say applicants may need to visit the RTO on the scheduled date with originals and the fee slip. 
Parivahan

13. Pass the LL test

Complete the test.

Once your application/test is approved, your Learner's Licence will be issued.

You can generally retrieve it through:

Learner Licence → Print Learner Licence (Form 3)

Enter your Application Number + DOB and submit. 
Parivahan

Part 2 — Learn and practise driving

Now you have your Learner's Licence.

Your LL is valid for 6 months, and you become eligible to apply for the new Driving Licence after 30 days. 
Parivahan

So use this period to practise the vehicle classes covered by your LL and prepare for the practical test.

Part 3 — Apply for the Permanent Driving Licence

After you've held your LL for at least 30 days, return to:

Sarathi Parivahan

Select Maharashtra again.

14. Choose New Driving Licence

On the Maharashtra portal, go to the Driving Licence section and choose:

New Driving Licence

You'll be asked for your existing:

Learner's Licence Number + Date of Birth

Enter them and continue.

Complete the New DL application form. The application corresponds to Form 4 for the permanent driving licence. 
Parivahan

15. Complete the required DL application steps

Check the vehicle class, applicant details and other information pulled from your LL.

Complete any document, declaration, photo/signature or other steps that Sarathi displays for your application.

Then pay the applicable DL/test fees through the portal and keep the receipt.

16. Book your driving test slot

Use the Appointments / DL Test Slot Booking option shown on Sarathi.

Select your RTO, choose an available date/time and confirm the appointment.

Parivahan provides online appointment scheduling for the driving competence test where the facility is available. 
Parivahan

17. Go to the RTO for your driving test

On the scheduled date, go to the relevant RTO with the documents/receipts specified on your acknowledgement.

The practical test is conducted by the competent authority.

You need to demonstrate that you can safely operate the relevant vehicle. Parivahan also says the applicant should bring the type of vehicle corresponding to the application for the test. 
Parivahan

If you're applying for more than one vehicle class, follow the RTO/Sarathi instructions for testing for those classes.

18. Pass the driving test

If you pass, the RTO processes your application for issuance of the Driving Licence.

Parivahan states that after successful completion of the competence test, the DL is issued and sent by Speed Post to the address provided.

Step 1 — Open the official Sarathi website

Sarathi Parivahan — Driving Licence Services

This is the Government of India's official portal. Don't use an agent or random third-party DL website.

Step 2 — Select your state

On the Select State Name screen:

Select → Maharashtra

The Maharashtra Sarathi portal should then open.

Step 3 — Start the Learner's Licence application

On the Maharashtra page, look at the top menu/navigation.

Choose:

Learner Licence → Application for New Learner's Licence

Depending on the current version of the portal, the wording may instead be Apply for New Learner Licence or similar. The official Parivahan instructions confirm the flow is State → Learner's Licence → New Learner's Licence application.

Save your Application Number when Sarathi generates it. You'll need it later for things like application status, payment, and downloading the LL.
