Go to the official government portal:

Sarathi Parivahan – Driving Licence Portal

1. Select Maharashtra

You'll see “Select State Name”.

Choose Maharashtra from the dropdown. This opens the Maharashtra Sarathi portal.

2. Start a new Learner's Licence application

On the Maharashtra portal, open:

Learner Licence → Application for New Learner's Licence

The exact wording/layout can vary slightly by state or portal update, but this is the official route specified by Parivahan. 
Parivahan

Read the instructions and press Continue.

3. Choose your applicant category

Because this is your first licence, choose the option indicating that you do not hold an existing Driving/Learner's Licence, if the portal asks.

Do not select an option for an existing DL unless you already have one.

4. Authentication

Sarathi may offer Aadhaar-based authentication depending on the services currently enabled for Maharashtra.

If Aadhaar authentication is offered and your Aadhaar details/mobile are suitable, it's usually the simplest route. Follow the OTP verification shown by Sarathi.

If you use a non-Aadhaar route, additional document verification/RTO steps may be required.

5. Fill in your personal information

Enter the requested information carefully, such as your name, date of birth, gender, parent/guardian details, address, contact information and other fields shown.

Keep spellings consistent with your supporting documents, especially your name, DOB and address.

6. Select your RTO

Choose the RTO applicable to your address/jurisdiction.

Be careful here: Parivahan says the RTO associated with an application can be changed before fee payment, so check it before paying. 
Parivahan

7. Select the vehicle class

This determines what you're getting licensed to drive.

For a normal personal car, you'll generally be looking for LMV (Light Motor Vehicle).

For motorcycles, the portal can show motorcycle categories depending on the type of vehicle/licence being requested.

If you want to drive both a car and motorcycle, make sure the appropriate classes are included in your LL application rather than accidentally applying only for one.

8. Complete the application

Check everything you've entered and submit the application.

Sarathi should generate an Application Number.

Save that number immediately — screenshot it or write it down. You'll use it for payment, application status, LL test and other services.

9. Upload the required documents

Depending on the Maharashtra workflow shown for your application, Sarathi may ask you to upload scanned documents.

Follow:

Upload Documents → Upload/Scan Documents

The exact document requirements shown by Sarathi take priority because services and requirements can vary by state/application. 
Parivahan

You'll generally need documentation establishing things such as age and address, plus any declarations/forms requested by the portal.

Form 1 is the physical-fitness self-declaration. Parivahan states Form 1A medical certificate is required for LL applicants aged 40 or above; other circumstances, such as certain vehicle categories, can also affect requirements, so follow what Sarathi generates for your application. 
Parivahan
+1

10. Photo/signature

Complete the photo and signature step if Sarathi asks you to upload or capture them online.

If the portal instead requires these to be captured/verified at the RTO, follow the instructions generated for your application.

11. Pay the LL fees

Open the fee/payment option for your application.

You'll normally enter your:

Application Number → Date of Birth → Calculate Fee

Then select the available payment method/gateway, complete CAPTCHA if shown and make the payment.

Keep the payment receipt and reference details. Sarathi also provides Verify Pay Status and Print Receipt functions. 
Sarathi Parivahan

12. Complete/Book the Learner's Licence test

The next step is the LL knowledge test, covering things such as road signs, traffic rules and basic driving regulations.

Depending on the services enabled for your application/state, Sarathi may provide an online LL test or require an appointment/visit.

For states/applications supporting the online test, Parivahan's route is:

Learner Licence → Online Learners' License Test (STALL)

Then enter your LL application details, DOB and password as requested. Parivahan notes that online LL testing is only available where the service is enabled. 
Parivahan

If Sarathi instead tells you to book an appointment/visit the RTO, follow that workflow and carry the original documents and fee receipt. The official LL instructions specifically say applicants may need to visit the RTO on the scheduled date with originals and the fee slip. 
Parivahan

13. Pass the LL test

Complete the test.

Once your application/test is approved, your Learner's Licence will be issued.

You can generally retrieve it through:

Learner Licence → Print Learner Licence (Form 3)

Enter your Application Number + DOB and submit. 
Parivahan

Part 2 — Learn and practise driving

Now you have your Learner's Licence.

Your LL is valid for 6 months, and you become eligible to apply for the new Driving Licence after 30 days. 
Parivahan

So use this period to practise the vehicle classes covered by your LL and prepare for the practical test.

Part 3 — Apply for the Permanent Driving Licence

After you've held your LL for at least 30 days, return to:

Sarathi Parivahan

Select Maharashtra again.

14. Choose New Driving Licence

On the Maharashtra portal, go to the Driving Licence section and choose:

New Driving Licence

You'll be asked for your existing:

Learner's Licence Number + Date of Birth

Enter them and continue.

Complete the New DL application form. The application corresponds to Form 4 for the permanent driving licence. 
Parivahan

15. Complete the required DL application steps

Check the vehicle class, applicant details and other information pulled from your LL.

Complete any document, declaration, photo/signature or other steps that Sarathi displays for your application.

Then pay the applicable DL/test fees through the portal and keep the receipt.

16. Book your driving test slot

Use the Appointments / DL Test Slot Booking option shown on Sarathi.

Select your RTO, choose an available date/time and confirm the appointment.

Parivahan provides online appointment scheduling for the driving competence test where the facility is available. 
Parivahan

17. Go to the RTO for your driving test

On the scheduled date, go to the relevant RTO with the documents/receipts specified on your acknowledgement.

The practical test is conducted by the competent authority.

You need to demonstrate that you can safely operate the relevant vehicle. Parivahan also says the applicant should bring the type of vehicle corresponding to the application for the test. 
Parivahan

If you're applying for more than one vehicle class, follow the RTO/Sarathi instructions for testing for those classes.

18. Pass the driving test

If you pass, the RTO processes your application for issuance of the Driving Licence.

Parivahan states that after successful completion of the competence test, the DL is issued and sent by Speed Post to the address provided. 
Parivahan

So the entire journey is basically:

Sarathi → Maharashtra → New Learner's Licence → application → documents → photo/signature → fees → LL test → LL issued → wait minimum 30 days → New Driving Licence → fees → book driving test → RTO practical test → pass → DL issued.

Yes. If you're applying for your first driving licence in Maharashtra, the website process has two stages:

Learner's Licence (LL) → wait at least 30 days → Permanent Driving Licence (DL) + driving test. Your LL remains valid for 6 months. 
Parivahan
+1

Part 1 — Apply for your Learner's Licence

Go to the official government portal:

Sarathi Parivahan – Driving Licence Portal

1. Select Maharashtra

You'll see “Select State Name”.

Choose Maharashtra from the dropdown. This opens the Maharashtra Sarathi portal.

2. Start a new Learner's Licence application

On the Maharashtra portal, open:

Learner Licence → Application for New Learner's Licence

The exact wording/layout can vary slightly by state or portal update, but this is the official route specified by Parivahan. 
Parivahan

Read the instructions and press Continue.

3. Choose your applicant category

Because this is your first licence, choose the option indicating that you do not hold an existing Driving/Learner's Licence, if the portal asks.

Do not select an option for an existing DL unless you already have one.

4. Authentication

Sarathi may offer Aadhaar-based authentication depending on the services currently enabled for Maharashtra.

If Aadhaar authentication is offered and your Aadhaar details/mobile are suitable, it's usually the simplest route. Follow the OTP verification shown by Sarathi.

If you use a non-Aadhaar route, additional document verification/RTO steps may be required.

5. Fill in your personal information

Enter the requested information carefully, such as your name, date of birth, gender, parent/guardian details, address, contact information and other fields shown.

Keep spellings consistent with your supporting documents, especially your name, DOB and address.

6. Select your RTO

Choose the RTO applicable to your address/jurisdiction.

Be careful here: Parivahan says the RTO associated with an application can be changed before fee payment, so check it before paying. 
Parivahan

7. Select the vehicle class

This determines what you're getting licensed to drive.

For a normal personal car, you'll generally be looking for LMV (Light Motor Vehicle).

For motorcycles, the portal can show motorcycle categories depending on the type of vehicle/licence being requested.

If you want to drive both a car and motorcycle, make sure the appropriate classes are included in your LL application rather than accidentally applying only for one.

8. Complete the application

Check everything you've entered and submit the application.

Sarathi should generate an Application Number.

Save that number immediately — screenshot it or write it down. You'll use it for payment, application status, LL test and other services.

9. Upload the required documents

Depending on the Maharashtra workflow shown for your application, Sarathi may ask you to upload scanned documents.

Follow:

Upload Documents → Upload/Scan Documents

The exact document requirements shown by Sarathi take priority because services and requirements can vary by state/application. 
Parivahan

You'll generally need documentation establishing things such as age and address, plus any declarations/forms requested by the portal.

Form 1 is the physical-fitness self-declaration. Parivahan states Form 1A medical certificate is required for LL applicants aged 40 or above; other circumstances, such as certain vehicle categories, can also affect requirements, so follow what Sarathi generates for your application. 
Parivahan
+1

10. Photo/signature

Complete the photo and signature step if Sarathi asks you to upload or capture them online.

If the portal instead requires these to be captured/verified at the RTO, follow the instructions generated for your application.

11. Pay the LL fees

Open the fee/payment option for your application.

You'll normally enter your:

Application Number → Date of Birth → Calculate Fee

Then select the available payment method/gateway, complete CAPTCHA if shown and make the payment.

Keep the payment receipt and reference details. Sarathi also provides Verify Pay Status and Print Receipt functions. 
Sarathi Parivahan

12. Complete/Book the Learner's Licence test

The next step is the LL knowledge test, covering things such as road signs, traffic rules and basic driving regulations.

Depending on the services enabled for your application/state, Sarathi may provide an online LL test or require an appointment/visit.

For states/applications supporting the online test, Parivahan's route is:

Learner Licence → Online Learners' License Test (STALL)

Then enter your LL application details, DOB and password as requested. Parivahan notes that online LL testing is only available where the service is enabled. 
Parivahan

If Sarathi instead tells you to book an appointment/visit the RTO, follow that workflow and carry the original documents and fee receipt. The official LL instructions specifically say applicants may need to visit the RTO on the scheduled date with originals and the fee slip. 
Parivahan

13. Pass the LL test

Complete the test.

Once your application/test is approved, your Learner's Licence will be issued.

You can generally retrieve it through:

Learner Licence → Print Learner Licence (Form 3)

Enter your Application Number + DOB and submit. 
Parivahan

Part 2 — Learn and practise driving

Now you have your Learner's Licence.

Your LL is valid for 6 months, and you become eligible to apply for the new Driving Licence after 30 days. 
Parivahan

So use this period to practise the vehicle classes covered by your LL and prepare for the practical test.

Part 3 — Apply for the Permanent Driving Licence

After you've held your LL for at least 30 days, return to:

Sarathi Parivahan

Select Maharashtra again.

14. Choose New Driving Licence

On the Maharashtra portal, go to the Driving Licence section and choose:

New Driving Licence

You'll be asked for your existing:

Learner's Licence Number + Date of Birth

Enter them and continue.

Complete the New DL application form. The application corresponds to Form 4 for the permanent driving licence. 
Parivahan

15. Complete the required DL application steps

Check the vehicle class, applicant details and other information pulled from your LL.

Complete any document, declaration, photo/signature or other steps that Sarathi displays for your application.

Then pay the applicable DL/test fees through the portal and keep the receipt.

16. Book your driving test slot

Use the Appointments / DL Test Slot Booking option shown on Sarathi.

Select your RTO, choose an available date/time and confirm the appointment.

Parivahan provides online appointment scheduling for the driving competence test where the facility is available. 
Parivahan

17. Go to the RTO for your driving test

On the scheduled date, go to the relevant RTO with the documents/receipts specified on your acknowledgement.

The practical test is conducted by the competent authority.

You need to demonstrate that you can safely operate the relevant vehicle. Parivahan also says the applicant should bring the type of vehicle corresponding to the application for the test. 
Parivahan

If you're applying for more than one vehicle class, follow the RTO/Sarathi instructions for testing for those classes.

18. Pass the driving test

If you pass, the RTO processes your application for issuance of the Driving Licence.

Parivahan states that after successful completion of the competence test, the DL is issued and sent by Speed Post to the address provided. 
Parivahan

So the entire journey is basically:

Sarathi → Maharashtra → New Learner's Licence → application → documents → photo/signature → fees → LL test → LL issued → wait minimum 30 days → New Driving Licence → fees → book driving test → RTO practical test → pass → DL issued.

Step 1 — Open the official Sarathi website

Sarathi Parivahan — Driving Licence Services

This is the Government of India's official portal. Don't use an agent or random third-party DL website.

Step 2 — Select your state

On the Select State Name screen:

Select → Maharashtra

The Maharashtra Sarathi portal should then open.

Step 3 — Start the Learner's Licence application

On the Maharashtra page, look at the top menu/navigation.

Choose:

Learner Licence → Application for New Learner's Licence

Depending on the current version of the portal, the wording may instead be Apply for New Learner Licence or similar. The official Parivahan instructions confirm the flow is State → Learner's Licence → New Learner's Licence application.

Step 4 — Follow the application

You'll then go through the LL application process: enter your details, choose the vehicle class you want (for example, motorcycle with gear and/or LMV for a car), complete the required document/photo steps shown for Maharashtra, pay the applicable fee, and complete the LL test/appointment process offered by the portal.

Once your Learner's Licence is issued, you can move on to the permanent DL stage after the required period. Parivahan says you need to have held a valid LL for at least 30 days before taking the driving competence test.

give me full process 

Yes. If you're applying for your first driving licence in Maharashtra, the website process has two stages:

Learner's Licence (LL) → wait at least 30 days → Permanent Driving Licence (DL) + driving test. Your LL remains valid for 6 months. 
Parivahan
+1

Part 1 — Apply for your Learner's Licence

Go to the official government portal:

Sarathi Parivahan – Driving Licence Portal

1. Select Maharashtra

You'll see “Select State Name”.

Choose Maharashtra from the dropdown. This opens the Maharashtra Sarathi portal.

2. Start a new Learner's Licence application

On the Maharashtra portal, open:

Learner Licence → Application for New Learner's Licence

The exact wording/layout can vary slightly by state or portal update, but this is the official route specified by Parivahan. 
Parivahan

Read the instructions and press Continue.

3. Choose your applicant category

Because this is your first licence, choose the option indicating that you do not hold an existing Driving/Learner's Licence, if the portal asks.

Do not select an option for an existing DL unless you already have one.

4. Authentication

Sarathi may offer Aadhaar-based authentication depending on the services currently enabled for Maharashtra.

If Aadhaar authentication is offered and your Aadhaar details/mobile are suitable, it's usually the simplest route. Follow the OTP verification shown by Sarathi.

If you use a non-Aadhaar route, additional document verification/RTO steps may be required.

5. Fill in your personal information

Enter the requested information carefully, such as your name, date of birth, gender, parent/guardian details, address, contact information and other fields shown.

Keep spellings consistent with your supporting documents, especially your name, DOB and address.

6. Select your RTO

Choose the RTO applicable to your address/jurisdiction.

Be careful here: Parivahan says the RTO associated with an application can be changed before fee payment, so check it before paying. 
Parivahan

7. Select the vehicle class

This determines what you're getting licensed to drive.

For a normal personal car, you'll generally be looking for LMV (Light Motor Vehicle).

For motorcycles, the portal can show motorcycle categories depending on the type of vehicle/licence being requested.

If you want to drive both a car and motorcycle, make sure the appropriate classes are included in your LL application rather than accidentally applying only for one.

8. Complete the application

Check everything you've entered and submit the application.

Sarathi should generate an Application Number.

Save that number immediately — screenshot it or write it down. You'll use it for payment, application status, LL test and other services.

9. Upload the required documents

Depending on the Maharashtra workflow shown for your application, Sarathi may ask you to upload scanned documents.

Follow:

Upload Documents → Upload/Scan Documents

The exact document requirements shown by Sarathi take priority because services and requirements can vary by state/application. 
Parivahan

You'll generally need documentation establishing things such as age and address, plus any declarations/forms requested by the portal.

Form 1 is the physical-fitness self-declaration. Parivahan states Form 1A medical certificate is required for LL applicants aged 40 or above; other circumstances, such as certain vehicle categories, can also affect requirements, so follow what Sarathi generates for your application. 
Parivahan
+1

10. Photo/signature

Complete the photo and signature step if Sarathi asks you to upload or capture them online.

If the portal instead requires these to be captured/verified at the RTO, follow the instructions generated for your application.

11. Pay the LL fees

Open the fee/payment option for your application.

You'll normally enter your:

Application Number → Date of Birth → Calculate Fee

Then select the available payment method/gateway, complete CAPTCHA if shown and make the payment.

Keep the payment receipt and reference details. Sarathi also provides Verify Pay Status and Print Receipt functions. 
Sarathi Parivahan

12. Complete/Book the Learner's Licence test

The next step is the LL knowledge test, covering things such as road signs, traffic rules and basic driving regulations.

Depending on the services enabled for your application/state, Sarathi may provide an online LL test or require an appointment/visit.

For states/applications supporting the online test, Parivahan's route is:

Learner Licence → Online Learners' License Test (STALL)

Then enter your LL application details, DOB and password as requested. Parivahan notes that online LL testing is only available where the service is enabled. 
Parivahan

If Sarathi instead tells you to book an appointment/visit the RTO, follow that workflow and carry the original documents and fee receipt. The official LL instructions specifically say applicants may need to visit the RTO on the scheduled date with originals and the fee slip. 
Parivahan

13. Pass the LL test

Complete the test.

Once your application/test is approved, your Learner's Licence will be issued.

You can generally retrieve it through:

Learner Licence → Print Learner Licence (Form 3)

Enter your Application Number + DOB and submit. 
Parivahan

Part 2 — Learn and practise driving

Now you have your Learner's Licence.

Your LL is valid for 6 months, and you become eligible to apply for the new Driving Licence after 30 days. 
Parivahan

So use this period to practise the vehicle classes covered by your LL and prepare for the practical test.

Part 3 — Apply for the Permanent Driving Licence

After you've held your LL for at least 30 days, return to:

Sarathi Parivahan

Select Maharashtra again.

14. Choose New Driving Licence

On the Maharashtra portal, go to the Driving Licence section and choose:

New Driving Licence

You'll be asked for your existing:

Learner's Licence Number + Date of Birth

Enter them and continue.

Complete the New DL application form. The application corresponds to Form 4 for the permanent driving licence. 
Parivahan

15. Complete the required DL application steps

Check the vehicle class, applicant details and other information pulled from your LL.

Complete any document, declaration, photo/signature or other steps that Sarathi displays for your application.

Then pay the applicable DL/test fees through the portal and keep the receipt.

16. Book your driving test slot

Use the Appointments / DL Test Slot Booking option shown on Sarathi.

Select your RTO, choose an available date/time and confirm the appointment.

Parivahan provides online appointment scheduling for the driving competence test where the facility is available. 
Parivahan

17. Go to the RTO for your driving test

On the scheduled date, go to the relevant RTO with the documents/receipts specified on your acknowledgement.

The practical test is conducted by the competent authority.

[ServiceWorker] Starting Agentic Pipeline for intent: Yep. If you're applying for your first Driving Licence in Maharashtra, think of it as two stages:

Learner's Licence (LL) → practice/wait 30 days → permanent Driving Licence (DL) + driving test.

You can handle the applications yourself through the official government portal—no agent is necessary.

Full website plan
Phase 1 — Get your documents ready

Before starting, keep your Aadhaar/mobile access and your basic identity, age, and address documents available. Maharashtra lists proof of age, proof of address, photographs, the applicable forms, and fees among the LL requirements. The exact documents requested by Sarathi can depend on the application route. 
Maharashtra Transport Department
+1

Also decide which vehicle classes you need. For a typical personal licence, that could mean a motorcycle category, LMV for a car, or both. Don't randomly select every category—the licence/testing requirements follow the classes you apply for.

Phase 2 — Apply for the Learner's Licence online

Start here:

Official Sarathi Parivahan portal

The official flow is essentially:

Sarathi → Select Maharashtra → Learner Licence → Application for New Learner Licence → fill application → continue through the required steps.

Parivahan notes that the exact flow can vary by state. 
Parivahan

During the application, you'll provide your personal details, address, vehicle class(es), etc. Depending on the Maharashtra/Sarathi flow presented to you, you'll then complete the required document/photo/signature or Aadhaar-related steps, fee payment and LL-test/appointment requirements.

Very important: save your Application Number when Sarathi generates it. You'll use it repeatedly.

Phase 3 — Complete the Learner's Licence test

The LL test checks things such as traffic signs, road rules and safe-driving basics. Maharashtra says candidates need 60% correct answers to pass; if unsuccessful, another test appointment can be taken. 
Maharashtra Transport Department

You can prepare using Maharashtra's official question bank:

Maharashtra LL Test Question Bank

Maharashtra also currently lists Issue of Learner License among its Sarathi-related faceless services. However, the exact process shown to you can depend on eligibility and the workflow Sarathi assigns your application. 
Maharashtra Transport Department

Once your LL is approved, Sarathi provides a Print Learner Licence (Form 3) service where applicable:

Learner Licence → Print Learner Licence (Form 3) → Application Number + DOB → Submit. 
Parivahan

Phase 4 — Practice and wait at least 30 days

Your Learner's Licence is valid for 6 months.

You become eligible to apply for the new Driving Licence after you've held the LL for at least 30 days. 
Parivahan
+1

Use that period to actually practise the vehicle classes you're going to test for.

Phase 5 — Apply for your permanent Driving Licence

After the 30-day minimum, return to:

Sarathi Parivahan

Select Maharashtra, then find the option for a New Driving Licence application.

You'll use your existing Learner's Licence details rather than creating another LL.

Complete the DL application and whatever steps Sarathi shows for your application, including fee payment and booking the driving-test slot/appointment.

For the permanent licence, Maharashtra lists Form 4, the Learner's Licence, age/address proof, photographs where applicable, fees, and valid documents for the vehicle used for the test among the requirements. 
Maharashtra Transport Department

Phase 6 — Take the driving test at the RTO

This part isn't online.

Go to the selected RTO/test location on your booked date with the required originals and the appropriate vehicle/documentation.

The testing authority checks whether you can safely control and operate the relevant vehicle. Parivahan states that you must have held a valid LL for at least 30 days before taking the competence test. 
Parivahan

Pass → licence gets processed.

If you fail, you'll need to follow the retest procedure shown by Sarathi/RTO.

Phase 7 — Receive/check your DL

After successfully passing and completing the process, the licence is issued. Parivahan states that successful applicants' licences are sent to the address furnished through Speed Post. 
Parivahan

So the whole journey is:

Documents → Sarathi → Maharashtra → New LL → application → verification/uploads → fees → LL test → get LL → wait ≥30 days + practise → New DL application → fees → driving-test slot → RTO driving test → pass → DL issued.

Learner's Licence (LL) → practice/wait 30 days → permanent Driving Licence (DL) + driving test.

You can handle the applications yourself through the official government portal—no agent is necessary.

Full website plan
Phase 1 — Get your documents ready

Before starting, keep your Aadhaar/mobile access and your basic identity, age, and address documents available. Maharashtra lists proof of age, proof of address, photographs, the applicable forms, and fees among the LL requirements. The exact documents requested by Sarathi can depend on the application route. 
Maharashtra Transport Department
+1

Also decide which vehicle classes you need. For a typical personal licence, that could mean a motorcycle category, LMV for a car, or both. Don't randomly select every category—the licence/testing requirements follow the classes you apply for.

Phase 2 — Apply for the Learner's Licence online

Start here:

Official Sarathi Parivahan portal

The official flow is essentially:

Sarathi → Select Maharashtra → Learner Licence → Application for New Learner Licence → fill application → continue through the required steps.

Parivahan notes that the exact flow can vary by state. 
Parivahan

During the application, you'll provide your personal details, address, vehicle class(es), etc. Depending on the Maharashtra/Sarathi flow presented to you, you'll then complete the required document/photo/signature or Aadhaar-related steps, fee payment and LL-test/appointment requirements.

Very important: save your Application Number when Sarathi generates it. You'll use it repeatedly.

Phase 3 — Complete the Learner's Licence test

The LL test checks things such as traffic signs, road rules and safe-driving basics. Maharashtra says candidates need 60% correct answers to pass; if unsuccessful, another test appointment can be taken. 
Maharashtra Transport Department

You can prepare using Maharashtra's official question bank:

Maharashtra LL Test Question Bank

Maharashtra also currently lists Issue of Learner License among its Sarathi-related faceless services. However, the exact process shown to you can depend on eligibility and the workflow Sarathi assigns your application. 
Maharashtra Transport Department

Once your LL is approved, Sarathi provides a Print Learner Licence (Form 3) service where applicable:

Learner Licence → Print Learner Licence (Form 3) → Application Number + DOB → Submit. 
Parivahan

Phase 4 — Practice and wait at least 30 days

Your Learner's Licence is valid for 6 months.

You become eligible to apply for the new Driving Licence after you've held the LL for at least 30 days. 
Parivahan
+1

Use that period to actually practise the vehicle classes you're going to test for.

Phase 5 — Apply for your permanent Driving Licence

After the 30-day minimum, return to:

Sarathi Parivahan

Select Maharashtra, then find the option for a New Driving Licence application.

You'll use your existing Learner's Licence details rather than creating another LL.

Complete the DL application and whatever steps Sarathi shows for your application, including fee payment and booking the driving-test slot/appointment.

For the permanent licence, Maharashtra lists Form 4, the Learner's Licence, age/address proof, photographs where applicable, fees, and valid documents for the vehicle used for the test among the requirements. 
Maharashtra Transport Department

Phase 6 — Take the driving test at the RTO

This part isn't online.

Go to the selected RTO/test location on your booked date with the required originals and the appropriate vehicle/documentation.

The testing authority checks whether you can safely control and operate the relevant vehicle. Parivahan states that you must have held a valid LL for at least 30 days before taking the competence test. 
Parivahan

Pass → licence gets processed.

If you fail, you'll need to follow the retest procedure shown by Sarathi/RTO.

Phase 7 — Receive/check your DL

After successfully passing and completing the process, the licence is issued. Parivahan states that successful applicants' licences are sent to the address furnished through Speed Post. 
Parivahan

So the whole journey is:

Documents → Sarathi → Maharashtra → New LL → application → verification/uploads → fees → LL test → get LL → wait ≥30 days + practise → New DL application → fees → driving-test slot → RTO driving test → pass → DL issued.

Yep. Here’s the full website process for Maharashtra, starting from zero and going all the way to your permanent Driving Licence (DL). The process has two stages: Learner’s Licence (LL) → Driving Licence (DL). Maharashtra currently lists both the faceless Learner’s Licence service and new Driving Licence application as live. 
Maharashtra Transport Department
+1

Stage 1 — Apply for your Learner’s Licence

Start on the official Sarathi portal:

Sarathi Parivahan – Driving Licence Services

1. Select Maharashtra

On the first page, find “Please select the State from where the service is to be taken” and choose Maharashtra.

You’ll then land on Maharashtra’s Sarathi services page.

2. Start the Learner’s Licence application

Look for Learner Licence / Learner License in the menu.

Choose the option for a new Learner’s Licence application. Depending on the current Sarathi interface, the wording can vary slightly, so follow the option referring to Application for New Learner Licence.

Maharashtra officially lists Issue of Learner License as a Sarathi faceless service. 
Maharashtra Transport Department

3. Choose the Aadhaar/faceless route if offered

Sarathi may ask whether you want to authenticate through Aadhaar.

If your Aadhaar details and Aadhaar-linked mobile number are available, the Aadhaar authentication/faceless route is generally the easiest option.

Complete the OTP verification when requested.

4. Fill in your application

Carefully check or enter your personal information, such as your name, date of birth, address and other requested details.

Make sure your details match your supporting documents, especially the spelling of your name and DOB.

5. Select the vehicle class

This part matters.

For a normal car, select:

LMV — Light Motor Vehicle

For a geared motorcycle, select the appropriate motorcycle with gear category shown by Sarathi.

If you want both car + geared motorcycle, select both relevant classes if the portal allows them in the same application.

Don’t choose transport/commercial categories unless you actually need a commercial/transport licence.

6. Submit the application and save the number

Once the initial application is submitted, Sarathi generates an Application Number.

Save this number immediately.

Take a screenshot or save the acknowledgement PDF because you’ll use the application number for things such as payments, application status and LL-related services.

7. Complete the required documents/forms

The portal will show what documents/forms are required for your application.

Maharashtra lists age, residence and citizenship proof among the LL requirements, along with the relevant forms and fee. 
Maharashtra Transport Department

Follow exactly what your Sarathi application asks you to upload or authenticate.

8. Pay the Learner’s Licence fee

Go to the Fee Payments stage when Sarathi shows it.

The Maharashtra fee page currently lists ₹151 per vehicle class + ₹50 LL test fee. Your portal-generated amount is the one to follow because your selected vehicle classes/services can change the total. 
Maharashtra Transport Department

Sarathi's payment system uses your Application Number + DOB and provides options to verify payment status and print the receipt. 
Sarathi

Save the payment receipt.

9. Complete the Learner’s Licence test

Follow the LL test option shown for your application. Depending on the workflow available to you, Sarathi may provide the online/faceless test process or require the applicable RTO workflow.

The LL test covers basic traffic rules, signs, road safety and driving regulations.

Maharashtra says you need 60% correct answers to pass the preliminary LL test. 
Maharashtra Transport Department

Sarathi also has an Online Learners’ License Test (STALL) service in states where it is available. 
Parivahan

10. Download your Learner’s Licence

After you've passed and the application is approved, return to Sarathi.

Go to:

Learner Licence → Print Learner Licence (Form 3)

Yep. If you're applying for your first driving licence in Maharashtra, you normally do it in two stages:

Learner's Licence (LL) → wait at least 30 days → Permanent Driving Licence (DL) + driving test. Maharashtra confirms that a permanent-DL test application can be made after holding the LL for 30 days. 
Maharashtra Transport Department
+1

I'll guide you through the actual website flow.

Part 1 — Get everything ready

For a normal private car and/or motorcycle licence, keep your Aadhaar/mobile and your age/address documents available. Maharashtra lists proof of residence, proof of age, citizenship proof, photographs and the prescribed forms among the LL requirements. 
Maharashtra Transport Department

For vehicle class, the common choices are:

MCWG — motorcycle with gear

MCWOG — motorcycle without gear

LMV — light motor vehicle, such as a private car

If you want to drive both a normal geared motorcycle and a car, you'll generally be looking for MCWG + LMV in the application.

Part 2 — Open the official Sarathi website

Go directly to:

Sarathi Parivahan — Driving Licence Services

This is the Government of India's Sarathi portal. The official procedure begins by opening Sarathi and selecting your state. 
Parivahan

Step 1: Select Maharashtra

On Select State Name, choose:

Maharashtra

Wait for the Maharashtra Sarathi page to load.

Step 2: Find the Learner Licence application

On the Maharashtra page, open Learner Licence.

Look for an option such as:

Application for New Learner Licence

or Apply for Learner Licence.

The exact wording/layout can vary because Sarathi services are customised by state. The official Parivahan instructions describe the route as State → Learner's Licence → Application for New Learner's Licence. 
Parivahan

Step 3: Read the instructions

You'll get an instructions page explaining the application process.

Read it, tick the declaration/checkbox if shown, and click Continue.

Step 4: Choose your applicant category

Because this is your first licence, select the option indicating that you do not currently hold a Driving Licence/Learner Licence, if that's what applies to you.

Don't select options such as Applicant holds Driving Licence unless you already have one.

Continue.

Part 3 — Aadhaar authentication

If Maharashtra offers Aadhaar-based authentication/faceless LL processing on your application, choose that route if your details are suitable. Maharashtra currently lists Issue of Learner License among its Sarathi-related faceless services. 
Maharashtra Transport Department

Typically you'll enter your Aadhaar number, consent to authentication, receive an OTP on the mobile linked with Aadhaar, and verify it.

Important: make sure the personal details you submit are correct. Don't casually change spelling, DOB or address just to make the application proceed.

If the portal instead routes you through a non-Aadhaar/RTO process, follow that workflow—the available flow can depend on the service and applicant.

Part 4 — Fill the LL application

You'll then complete/verify the application details.

Check things like your:

Name → DOB → gender → address → contact details → qualification/other requested information

If Aadhaar authentication populated some fields automatically, verify them carefully.

Then select your RTO/licensing authority when requested. Choose the appropriate office for your jurisdiction; don't pick another RTO simply because it has an earlier appointment.

Step 5: Select vehicle class

This part matters.

If you want a licence for a geared motorcycle, select MCWG.

If you want a private car, select LMV.

If you need both and the portal permits both in the same application, select:

MCWG + LMV

Check the description displayed next to each code before confirming.

Then submit/continue.

Step 6: Save your application number

After successful submission, Sarathi generates an Application Number.

Save it immediately—screenshot it or write it down.

You'll use the application number for payments, application status, appointments and other services.

Part 5 — Documents, photo/signature and declarations

The portal may ask you to complete additional stages such as:

Upload Documents → Upload Photo/Signature → LL Slot Booking → Fee Payment

The exact stages displayed depend on the Maharashtra workflow and whether Aadhaar authentication/faceless services are available for your case. Parivahan specifically notes that document-upload functionality depends on state customisation. 
Parivahan

Complete every item that Sarathi marks as pending.

Maharashtra's published LL requirements include Form 1, Form 2, photographs, residence proof, age proof, citizenship proof and fees, although your online/Aadhaar workflow may handle some of these electronically. 
Maharashtra Transport Department

Part 6 — Pay the LL fee

When Fee Payment becomes available, enter/confirm your application details and calculate the fee.

Sarathi's payment instructions are essentially:

Application number + DOB → Calculate Fee → payment option/gateway → CAPTCHA → Proceed → payment. 
Sarathi Parivahan

Save the receipt after successful payment.

Maharashtra currently publishes the learner licence fee as ₹151 per vehicle class plus ₹50 test fee, but use the amount calculated by Sarathi for your actual application because the total can depend on the selected services/classes. 
Maharashtra Transport Department

Part 7 — Learner Licence test

You now need to complete the LL test according to the workflow Sarathi gives you.

The Maharashtra Motor Vehicle Department says the learner applicant must complete the online application and preliminary test; its published procedure says 60% correct answers are required to pass. 
Maharashtra Transport Department

Study road signs, traffic lights, road markings, right-of-way, overtaking, parking, basic traffic laws and safe driving.

If your application provides the online LL test service, Parivahan's route is:

Sarathi → Maharashtra → Learner Licence → Online Learners' License Test → application details → Login.

Online LL testing is only available where the state/service supports it. 
Parivahan

Once you pass and the application is approved, you get your Learner's Licence.

Part 8 — Download your LL

Return to Sarathi:

Sarathi Parivahan

Select Maharashtra → Learner Licence → Print Learner Licence (Form 3).

Enter your Application Number + Date of Birth, submit and download/print the LL where that service is available. That's also the current procedure given by Parivahan. 
Parivahan
+1

Part 9 — Apply for your permanent Driving Licence

Getting the LL isn't the end. Now you practise driving legally under the learner conditions.

You must hold the valid Learner's Licence for at least 30 days before appearing for the permanent driving-licence competence test. 
Parivahan
+1

Once you're eligible, return to:

Sarathi Parivahan

Select:

Maharashtra → Driving Licence → Apply for Driving Licence

Enter the requested Learner Licence/application details and DOB, authenticate as requested, complete the DL application, select the relevant vehicle class(es), pay the applicable fee and book your DL test slot.

The permanent licence application is Form 4 and is made for the vehicle class covered by the LL. 
Parivahan
+1

Part 10 — Take the driving test

Go to the selected RTO/test location on your appointment date with the required originals and a suitable vehicle for the class you're being tested on.

The competence test checks whether you can safely control and drive the relevant vehicle. Parivahan states that the applicant should bring the type of vehicle to which the application relates and demonstrate the required driving ability to the testing authority. 
Parivahan

Pass the test → application gets approved → permanent Driving Licence is issued.

So your full journey is:

Sarathi → Maharashtra → New Learner Licence → application/Aadhaar → select RTO → MCWG/LMV → documents → fee → LL test → LL issued → practise ≥30 days → Apply for Driving Licence → pay/book slot → driving test → DL issued.
